newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Spain looking to host NATO enlargement summit.
newsitem.headline: Spain looking to host NATO enlargement summit.

text.p: Spain has begun testing the attitude of its 15 fellow NATO members to the idea that it should host the summit on enlargement pencilled in for the middle of next year, alliance sources said on Thursday.

"There is no formal proposition. Rather Spain is quietly testing the water with the other NATO members. If no one says no then it will probably make a formal bid," one alliance diplomat said. "So far no one has rejected it outright."
Sources at the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation said the move could have considerable merits.
Spain has decided to end its isolation from the alliance's military structure and take part fully in the decision-making process. Giving it a key NATO summit would be a pat on the back.
At the same time, NATO Secretary General Javier Solana is a Spaniard who is seen as having performed creditably in his first year in the job.
France had wanted to host the summit that must decide on the first countries from east and central Europe which will be invited to join the alliance.

But the row between France and the United States over command of NATO's southern headquarters in Naples, Italy -- France wants it to go to a European but the United States refuses -- has ruled Paris out, alliance diplomats said.
Brussels could host the summit, but it was the venue for the last meeting of NATO leaders in January 1994 and there is a feeling the next such meeting should be held somewhere else.
To date no other nation has indicated a desire to host the next summit, although one alliance source said there had been some mention of the possibility of it being in Amsterdam.

However, the Dutch will have their work cut out in the first six months of next year as they take over the presidency of the European Union and are due to host a key EU summit in June on reform of the bloc.
An alliance spokesman said the speculation was all premature.
"We haven't even decided on a summit yet. When that decision is taken the decision on the venue will be made at the same time," he said.

NATO foreign ministers are due to meet in Brussels on Tuesday and Wednesday next week. Alliance sources said there would doubtless be some discussion on the margins of the meeting on the summit issue.
